claims.text: Controlled heat treatment can selectively modify local atomic-ordering fluctuations and phase-boundary character in the target alloy.
Tuning local atomic-ordering fluctuations at phase boundaries enhances magnetostructural coupling.
The enhanced magnetostructural coupling enables a sharp, reversible magnetic phase transition at low applied fields.
The resulting low-field transition produces a strong magnetocaloric response.
The proposed microstructural tuning preserves rapid heat exchange.
The proposed microstructural tuning maintains low magnetic hysteresis.
The initial alloy is a chemically disordered, homogeneous FCC rare-earth-free high-entropy alloy.
Enhanced local-ordering fluctuations create a more uniform magnetic-exchange environment.
A more uniform exchange environment lowers the energy barrier for magnetic-domain reorientation.
Lowering the domain-reorientation barrier facilitates a rapid and reversible magnetic phase transition.
The inherent disordered matrix supports rapid heat exchange.
The inherent disordered matrix provides mechanical stability during cyclic operation.
Heat treatment will produce a sharper magnetic transition than in the untreated alloy.
Heat treatment will shift the reversible magnetic transition to lower applied fields.
Heat treatment will reduce magnetic hysteresis relative to the untreated control.
Heat treatment will maintain thermal transport and mechanical integrity during cyclic operation.
The untreated FCC alloy has broader magnetic transitions than the proposed heat-treated state.
The untreated alloy has higher magnetic hysteresis than the proposed heat-treated state.
The untreated alloy has less efficient heat exchange than the proposed heat-treated state.
The effect is confined to FCC rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys near room temperature under low-to-moderate fields and may not extend to other structures or extreme temperatures and fields.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described as a homogeneous single FCC phase, while the intervention and mediator presuppose microstructural phase boundaries. No second phase or heat-treatment-induced phase formation is specified to account for such boundaries.

The prediction says rapid heat exchange is maintained relative to treatment, whereas the baseline is described as having less efficient heat exchange. This makes it unclear whether thermal performance is expected to remain unchanged or improve.
